OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 06/09/2025

Dear Colleague,

Ankylosing spondylitis follow-up. Mr. Burgos remains on adalimumab 40 mg every two weeks and sulfasalazine 1,000 mg twice daily, taking both as prescribed. Low back pain persists and is still worse on waking. No eye redness or pain since we last saw him. No diarrhea or abdominal pain. No infections.

Allergies: NKDA.

Exam: tenderness over the sacroiliac joints; lumbar flexion reduced, similar to prior.

Monitoring labs reviewed — stable.

Plan: continue current therapy and home exercise program. Labs every three months. Return in six months or sooner as needed.

Rheumatology

reports.text:
EXAM: Lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints, radiographs.
INDICATION: Ankylosing spondylitis, progressive low back pain.
COMPARISON: Sacroiliac joint radiographs 01/23/2024.
FINDINGS: Changes at both sacroiliac joints suggest sclerosis and fusion. Lumbar vertebral bodies are normally aligned with normal height. Disc spaces are preserved. No fracture or destructive lesion.
reports.conclusion: Findings suggestive of bilateral sacroiliac joint sclerosis and fusion.

OUTSIDE RHEUMATOLOGY — FOLLOW-UP
Date of service: 01/27/2026

Dear Colleague,

Mr. Burgos is a 29-year-old man with ankylosing spondylitis, diagnosed in January 2024, and beta thalassemia minor, seen for continuing care. He describes chronic, dull, deep pain across the lower spine and both hips that has gradually worsened over the past two years. It is worse in the morning or after he has been still for a while and better with activity. More recently, morning stiffness has been lasting about an hour before it eases. No trauma or unusual strain. When asked, he described a few episodes of eye redness and discomfort in recent months that cleared without treatment. No fevers, chills or weight loss.

Medications: adalimumab 40 mg subcutaneously every two weeks; sulfasalazine 1,000 mg twice daily.
Allergies: no known drug allergies.
Family history: father with ankylosing spondylitis, who had back surgery in his forties.
Social: software engineer; describes himself as mostly sedentary now.

Examination: Gait normal. Lumbar flexion decreased and Schober's test positive. Chest expansion reduced. Tender over the sacroiliac joints.

Laboratory: inflammatory markers elevated. Rheumatoid factor negative. ANA negative.

Imaging: radiographs of the lumbar spine and sacroiliac joints today show changes suggestive of sclerosis and fusion of the sacroiliac joints.

Impression: ankylosing spondylitis with progressive symptoms on adalimumab and sulfasalazine; intermittent eye symptoms.

Plan: continue adalimumab and sulfasalazine at current doses. Daily stretching and mobility work. Your office to continue CBC and CMP every three months. Return in six months.

Rheumatology
